the MVDR method is a good estimator, but that the performance of the method depends on the number of snapshots, the number of sensors, the SNR, and the signal-to-interference ratio.
the MVDR spectrum estimator is very robust with respect to the perturbations in signal model, the noise covariance matrix and the finite data effects.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the performance analysis of MVDR spectrum estimator in this thesis has been carried out.
the MVDR estimator is a very good method to use in the case of a large signal to noise ratio and when the noise covariance matrix is known with a high degree of precision.
the MVDR estimator has a good performance when the noise covariance matrix is estimated from the data and the signal is not known.
The main takeaway from our work is that
for a fixed number of snapshots and a fixed number of sensors, the MVDR estimator is not a consistent estimator.
the MVDR spectrum estimator has a high bias for a small number of snapshots.
the performance of the MVDR spectrum estimator is highly sensitive to perturbations in both the signal and noise model parameters.
